s10.old: - **KEY PRINCIPLE (cost many rounds): rank = INFLUENCE; per-category stance = ALIGNMENT. Two separate axes** (see [[influence-vs-alignment-axes]]). A high-activity OPPONENT (e.g. AOC, Welch: prolific consumer-finance cosponsors, anti-CU) will rank decently on influence; that is fine: the stance layer is the friend/foe filter, and the optimizer won't fund opponents. Do NOT make the rank pure-influence-led as the ONLY view (user: "that does not reveal underdogs"): the **Moneyball point is undervaluation**. Underdogs surface in the SEPARATE undervaluation/efficiency view (Intrinsic/Visibility/Undervaluation/Underdog-rank columns + the optimizer), which the influence-weighted rank does not erase.
s10.why: "(see [[influence-vs-alignment-axes]])" names another note

Earlier this churned when leg was a big driver, but committee 0.40 now anchors the board so it is well-behaved. s10.old: - **Committee/Influence pillar:** `Blended Model!R` (col18, Influence%) = **committee_raw / MAX(committee_raw)** (`apply_committee_fix.py`), NOT the old double-percentile: percentile flattened a backbencher (score 2.5) to the 90th %ile next to chairs, so prolific juniors (Byron Donalds) ranked top-10. The normalized raw score distinguishes leadership: Crapo No. 1 (Banking+Finance+JCT), Tim Scott No. 2; Donalds No. 8 -> No. 14. Source = `Committee Data` relevance-tiered seats (Highly/Moderately/Slightly -> score; Small Business unified to Moderately).

s10.old: **COALITION DETERMINISM BUG (big one):** `per_topic_coalition.py` was non-deterministic even at fixed `random.seed`: two same-seed runs differed $12.6M. Cause: cascade frontier built from **sets** (`dict.fromkeys(Aseeds,...)`), and Python per-process **hash randomization** varies set iteration order, so random draws were consumed in different order. Fix: `sorted(Aseeds)/sorted(Bseeds)` in cascade (line ~35) + **Common Random Numbers** (`random.seed(1000003*SEED+it)` per MC iteration in `spread()`, so base and every `spread({n})` share draws, so marginal isolates the true effect) + `SEED`/`MC` now env-configurable. Now same-seed = byte-identical ($0). **Scenario protocol: always run baseline + perturbed at the SAME seed, so deltas are exact with zero MC noise.** Residual cross-seed variance (about $13M between seed99/199 at MC=20) is baseline-credibility only (which seed picked), irrelevant to same-seed deltas; bump MC or seed-ensemble later if the baseline itself needs to be less arbitrary. `per_topic_flip` is already deterministic (greedy LT, no MC).
s10.why: "seed-ensemble later" is time

s10.old: **Co-sponsor route finder BUILT + validated** (`cosponsor_route.py`): seeds = champions, edge-activation greedy (tree-reach spread, edge cost = CEDGE/p so weak ties cost more), out-degree K=5, Pareto front via risk-aversion lambda sweep. Fixed a value-inversion bug (added positive-value guard `if -nval<=0: break`). Validated: Mortgage max-spread $419k / +5.6 / risk 0.59 vs low-risk $33k / +1.2 / risk 0.39 (distinct Pareto points); **Interchange has NO reliable routes** (champions weakly tied, all p about 0.10, so don't run a co-sponsor campaign there). LT-priming + sheet-sync + MC-upgrade + full audit + reorg were then DONE (next section). Caveat: tree-reach spread is first-order/conservative (ignores cascade reinforcement); it could be upgraded to MC cascade. Remaining step 3 at that time: LT-priming calc; incremental D* Lite replanning; live Moneyball-sheet tab (COM write-back + cell-change replan). Audits still clean (22/22 + 11/11).
s10.why: "(next section)" is ## Step-3 finish + REORG, which follows ## Step 3 in 2026-06-feature-melange-scenario-model-build as in the note

s10.old: - **DOES IT RUN SCENARIOS? NO end-to-end runner.** Pieces existed (money_response computes shift + defection; scenario_diff compares; make_baseline freezes; sheet_sync detects changed topics) but NOTHING applied a shock, propagated net_lean, regenerated data, re-ran flip/coalition and diffed in one command. The missing piece = a scenario runner (OFFERED to build; built next).
s10.why: "built next" is time

s10.old: - **HONEST LIMITATIONS:** (1) CU spends only act via conversion/defection: no gradual winnability in the coalition cascade (that is the FLIP model); a non-converting CU spend shows about 0 effect. (2) The 18 low-receipt floor members (incl. Grijalva) defect too easily (the receipts-floor artifact). (3) The runner is ONE-SHOT (apply, observe); the ADAPTIVE optimizer (Golovin-Krause: greedily CHOOSE the moves to maximize influence under budget, observing realized defections) is the natural next layer, NOT built at that point.
s10.why: "the natural next layer" is a sequence in time

s10.old: - **SYSTEM STATE at that point:** stance (3D) -> flip (LT, capacity-aware) + coalition (competitive IC) + electoral (contest/defend) + routes (RELINK Pareto) + priming (LT) + money-response (defections) + scenario runner (both models) + adaptive optimizer (Golovin-Krause), all in Melange Systems, 26/26. Only the DASHBOARD UI remained (the roadmap's last item; see [[2026-06-feature-melange-dashboard-ui-evolution]] and [[melange-dashboard]]).
s10.why: "see [[2026-06-feature-melange-dashboard-ui-evolution]] and [[melange-dashboard]]" names other notes

s10.old: - **H2 (FIXED):** scenario per-topic rows were below the MC noise floor (std about 0.75-1.05 vs 0.3 threshold), giving impossible "competitor money helped CU" signs. Root cause: the cascade drew `random.random()` in activation order, so changing one member desynced the whole stream (CRN failure). Fix: splitmix64 `_sm(it,u,v)` edge-keyed draws, i.e. true CRN, so baseline vs scenario differ ONLY by the real perturbation. The comp shock is now clean: coalition -3.2, only same-sign rows. (budget_frontier.py had the same latent order-dependence, patched there only by non-monotone clamping; fixed later by HIGH-1.)
s10.why: "below the MC noise floor" is a threshold; "fixed later by HIGH-1" is time

s10.old: - **H3 (FIXED, later REVERSED, see below):** members with NO FEC data had ind=0, so b about 0 and pflip about 1 ("missing" misread as "no industry opposition"); 11 of 63 ranked top-50 winnability, inflating the base (215.92). Fix: impute the industry baseline (median of members WITH data) for zero-`total` members in flip_model.py + per_topic_flip.py; `fm.nodata` flags them. Base now realistic 186.50; 0 data-less in top-20. CAUGHT a follow-on: the scenario flip channel mixed imputed `fm.ind0` (baseline) with raw local `ind` (scenario), so the comp shock showed +28 winnability; fixed via `ind_flip = fm.ind0 + (ind-ind0_raw)` (one footing).
s10.why: "(FIXED, later REVERSED, see below)" is ## FEC data-quality assessment + HIGH-3 reversal, which follows the audit sections in 2026-06-troubleshooting-melange-model-audits as in the note
